summary_paragraph: A 55-year-old woman was admitted for recurrent nausea and vomiting five days after laparoscopic repair of a colonic mesenteric defect. Initial evaluation, including CT imaging, ruled out postoperative complications or bowel obstruction. Symptoms were attributed to a flare of chronic gastroparesis. She was managed with NG tube placement, IV fluids, and antiemetics, showing improvement within 24 hours. The NG tube was removed on hospital day two, and her diet was advanced successfully. Her gastroenterologist recommended continued dromperidone and a low-fat, small-meal diet. She was discharged home on day three with stable vital signs, no nausea, and a plan to follow up with her primary care provider and gastroenterologist. No medication changes were made except for reducing omeprazole from 40 mg to 20 mg daily.
